_comment: ADR 0702/0722 — the SHRINK-ONLY baseline of event types whose persisted payload does not
validate against the corpus $def its own _typeIndex names. Measured by
scripts/audit-event-payloads.mjs over a full backend suite run.
A type NOT listed here that starts violating FAILS the gate (a new wire gap).
A type listed here that stops violating ALSO fails — delete its line; a stale
admission is the thing that makes a ratchet stop ratcheting.
Types, not counts: the sample count varies with test ordering and flake, and a
gate that moves for reasons unrelated to the code teaches people to re-baseline it.
ADR 0725/0726 (2026-09-18, measurement #3: 1324 host samples / 50 types): 30 -> 2 admitted; 797 -> 7 wire errors.
`runOrchestrator.decided`: RFC 0007 §D requires the host to emit `next-worker` THEN `terminate` in a loop
topology, and `conformance-dispatch-loop`'s fixture supplies no child workflow — so the default plan's
`next-worker` carries `nextWorkerIds: []`, which `orchestrator-decision.schema.json` refuses (`minItems: 1`).
The MUST wins over the schema nicety: collapsing the plan to a single `terminate` fixes the payload and REDS
the scenario (measured 2026-09-18). Reported to the steward as a corpus mismatch; admitted here until it is settled.
2026-10-10 (ADR 0858 P4): the corpus SETTLED it — `v2-dispatch-loop` requires every decision to be one
OrchestratorDecision branch and does not port the v1 pair. The default plan is now a single `terminate`, so
this host's supervisor records no invalid decision. The type stays admitted because core.dispatch records
whatever decision it is handed, and `dispatch-iteration-counter.test.ts` hands it the forward-compat kind
`noop` (no branch accepts it). Measured on a targeted sample: `noop` is the only remaining violating shape.
2026-09-29: `approval.overridden` DELETED — it now validates: stored in the closed v1 shape and projected onto the v2 alias at egress (approvalOverriddenProjection.ts, openwop#1742 follow-on).
